title: Centre of Mass and Centre of Gravity
notes: **Centre of mass (CM):** the point where the entire mass of a body can be considered to be concentrated for translational motion. $\vec{r}_{CM} = \frac{\sum m_i \vec{r}_i}{\sum m_i}$.
**Centre of gravity (CG):** the point where the entire weight of a body can be considered to act. For uniform gravity, CG coincides with CM.
**Symmetry shortcut:** for symmetric bodies with uniform density, CM lies on the axis or plane of symmetry. For a uniform rod, CM is at its midpoint; for a uniform disc, at its centre.
**Why CM matters:** external forces cause the CM to accelerate according to $\vec{F}_{ext} = M\vec{a}_{CM}$, regardless of internal forces.
**Difference:** CM depends only on mass distribution; CG depends on the external gravitational field. In a non-uniform field, they can differ.
